title: Outcomes from Gifted Education Programme, and Rationale and Plans for Programme Revamp
what_it_is: Outcomes from Gifted Education Programme, and Rationale and Plans for Programme Revamp

sections.label: GEP change and class sizes
sections.summary: Questions ask why the GEP change is not elective by ability, and about primary class sizes in and outside the GEP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education why the recently announced change in the Gifted Education Programme is not designed into a system where students can elect their choices of subject levels based on their ability, gifting and interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what is the average class size for primary school students in the same cohort (i) enrolled in the existing Gifted Education Programme (GEP) (ii) enrolled in schools offering the existing GEP but are not part of the GEP; and (b) how are average class sizes expected to change with the changes made to the GEP.

sections.label: Opportunities for specific-area abilities
sections.summary: Instead of a uniform GEP based on general abilities, opportunities can be offered for higher abilities in specific areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Instead of a uniform GEP for selected students based on their general abilities in multiple areas, we can now also offer opportunities for those with higher abilities in specific areas.

sections.label: Higher-ability learners stay in schools
sections.summary: From the Primary 4 batch in 2027, higher-ability learners remain in their schools for school-based development without disrupting learning environments and social bonds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: From the Primary 4 batch in 2027, higher-ability learners will remain in their schools and benefit from school-based development, without having to disrupt their learning environments and the social bonds they have formed.

sections.label: Broadened access across all schools
sections.summary: Access to higher-ability programmes broadens from 7% to 10% of each cohort, with after-school modules open to eligible students from all schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: With the broadening of access to programmes for higher-ability learners in all schools from 7% to 10% of each cohort and after-school modules being accessible to eligible students from all schools, students will be able to benefit from the new approach regardless of the school they attend.

sections.label: Class sizing and broader support
sections.summary: Typical class size is unchanged, but schools can size classes for programmes and learning support, broadening support for higher-ability learners regardless of background.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: With this new approach, while there will be no change in the typical class size in schools, schools are able to size classes accordingly for the school-based programmes and after-school modules for higher-ability learners, as well as for learners who need more learning support, to ensure that the programmes achieve the intended outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Dr Wan Rizal also asked about strengthening access to quality education and support for all students regardless of their backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: These changes to the GEP will indeed broaden the support for higher-ability learners and provide more opportunities for them to maximise their potential, regardless of their background.

sections.label: Looking at student interests
sections.summary: The new approach looks at students, their interests and where they have strengths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In the new approach, what we are saying is that we look at the students, we look at what they are interested in, where they have strengths in.

sections.label: Clustering students by ability
sections.summary: The vision is to cluster students of generally the same abilities in the same domain for more effective teaching and learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: What we want to do in our vision going forward is that we are able to cluster the students of generally the same abilities in the same domain for more effective teaching and learning.

sections.label: MOE grouping by similar abilities
sections.summary: Singapore avoids mixing all abilities and segregating by interest, grouping students of similar abilities for selected topics and subjects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is why in Singapore, we have moved away from either of the extremes: one extreme is where we mix people of all abilities together and put them in the same class, regardless of abilities and interests; the other extreme is to segregate everyone just according to their specific interest and they never mix with other people with different interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We want the best of both worlds and this is how we have organised the MOE system – which is that for selected topics and subjects, we will group the students of similar abilities together so that it is easier and more manageable for the teachers to teach in a much more focused way.

sections.label: Class size context
sections.summary: Class sizes are generally organised on average between 30 and 40 people, depending on primary to secondary school levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I want to lay out the context of what we mean by class size in today's Singapore education context.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It is true that we organise our class sizes generally on average between 30 and 40 people, depending on primary school to secondary school levels.

sections.label: Class size not main determinant
sections.summary: OECD reports and overseas studies indicate the main determinant of education quality is not necessarily class size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If we look at the OECD reports and if we look at many of the studies overseas, the main determinant of the quality of our education system, as I explained yesterday during the Adjournment Motion, is not necessarily the class size.

sections.label: Tilting the curve
sections.summary: If the average cannot be changed, the approach is to tilt the curve without compromising quality when expanding numbers.

sentences.text: If we expand the numbers, we do not want to compromise the quality.
So, if we cannot change the average, what we need to do is what I call, we "tilt the curve".

sections.label: Technology adaptive training system
sections.summary: The conventional trilemma can be broken by leveraging technology to use an adaptive training system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If you have scale and you are affordable, chances are that the quality is not very good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But there is a way for us to break this conventional trilemma and, that is, how we leverage technology to use an adaptive training system.

sections.label: Mass customisation through technology
sections.summary: The pedagogy of one means mass customisation according to students' diverse abilities, complemented by technology, to break the conventional trilemma of scale, quality and affordability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Actually, it is not so far-fetched because the pedagogy of one means mass customisation according to the diverse abilities of our students, complemented by technology using artificial intelligence, data science and the science of learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is the vision of how we want to go forward to break the conventional trilemma, whereby we have finite numbers of quality teachers that will allow us to scale, achieve quality and make sure that it is affordable.

sections.label: Purpose of selection
sections.summary: Selection for higher-ability or differently-abled students is not to better prepare them for conventional exams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The purpose of selection for these higher-ability, or differently-abled students, is not to better prepare them for the conventional exams.

sections.label: Mathematics modules and leaving
sections.summary: For Mathematics, students may be exposed to different concepts and challenges, and there is no stigma in leaving a module found unsuitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Likewise, for Mathematics, we may expose the student to different kinds of concepts, different kinds of challenges to see how they respond to these.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We want to make sure that the student understands that when they join a module, there is no stigma to leave the module if they find it unsuitable for themselves or if they want to go and take time to pursue other things during that phase of their life.

sections.label: Children's diverse abilities
sections.summary: Children should understand and appreciate their diverse abilities and develop confidence to use them to contribute to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Let us help our children understand and appreciate their diverse abilities, find confidence in developing those abilities so that, in time to come, they can make the best use of those abilities to make a contribution to Singapore.
